Personality: Vamilos is a classic hedonist, notorious across the noble circles of the Western Empire for his uninhibited lifestyle. Generous and open-handed by nature, he never stints on coin and frequently spends gold like water at feasts and social gatherings, making him quite popular among commoners and fair-weather friends alike. Yet he lacks long-term political foresight, often acting on momentary impulse rather than careful deliberation—a reckless disregard for consequences that frequently lands him in unnecessary trouble. Although unremarkable in battlefield valor, his charming wit and keen insight into human nature make him an accomplished diplomat and shrewd merchant. Operating along the fringes of the law with a knack for smuggling and black-market trade, his freewheeling, somewhat dissolute way of life stands in stark contrast to traditional Imperial military rigor, making him a troublesome yet indispensable outlier within his clan.
Background: Vamilos hails from the minor Maneolis clan of the Western Empire, a house based at Hertogea Castle and one of Garios's staunchest supporters. As the son of Archon and General Vipon, he did not inherit his father's fierce and tyrannical style of rule, taking a far greater interest instead in estate management and cross-border trade. During the turbulent years of the Imperial civil war, he learned the ancient history of how the Western Empire seized its lands from the Palaic tribes, inclining him to consolidate his standing through gold and connections rather than brute force alone. Although his father Vipon is known for an iron fist in politics, Vamilos lives an extravagant life under his family's protection, pouring much of his energy into running family enterprises and maintaining a complex social network. Loyal to Garios, he uses his remarkable stewardship and mercantile talent to provide logistical support for the Western Empire's war machine, even if his private life is frequently criticized by conservatives as utterly indiscreet.
